binders: n is universally quantified over all natural numbers, including 0.
ell is an arbitrary function Fin n -> Real, equivalently an arbitrary real n-tuple.
f is an arbitrary function Fin n -> Real, equivalently an arbitrary real n-tuple.
hypotheses: The signed coordinatewise-product sum S = sum over i in Fin n of ell(i) f(i) is nonzero.
conclusions: 1 <= (sum over i in Fin n of |ell(i) f(i)|) / |sum over i in Fin n of ell(i) f(i)|.
mathematical_definitions: Let I_n = Fin n, identified with the n indices 0, 1, ..., n-1.
Define S = sum over i in I_n of ell(i) f(i).
Define A = sum over i in I_n of |ell(i) f(i)|.
LocalDef002 ell f = S and LocalDef001 ell f = A/|S|.
All absolute values are ordinary scalar real absolute values; no vector norm is explicitly present.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every natural-number dimension n and every pair of real n-tuples ell and f, if the sum of their coordinatewise products is nonzero, then the sum of the absolute values of those products, divided by the absolute value of their sum, is at least 1.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: No positivity assumption is imposed on n. When n = 0, both sums are empty and hence equal to 0, so the hypothesis is impossible and the proposition is vacuous.
For any n, the proposition makes no claim when the signed sum S is zero, including cases where nonzero products cancel.

Under the hypothesis S != 0, the denominator |S| is strictly positive, so the asserted quotient does not involve division by zero. Lean's real division is nevertheless a total operation outside this guarded case.
The statement concerns finite real tuples and exact real arithmetic only; it does not encode floating-point computation, approximation, rounding, or error bounds.
There are no assumptions that ell or f is nonnegative, normalized, bounded, or nonzero individually.
The statement provides no equality characterization, strictness criterion, or information beyond the non-strict lower bound.
